correctness.rationale: Constructed explicit mutually inverse pointed-graph maps fixing an entire spanning tree, with edge-path backtrack homotopies also relative to that tree. Coordinatewise homotopies preserve the condition that every anchor is attained, since anchors are fixed throughout. In the loop-adjoined CW graph, every loop boundary is zero integrally; grouping product cells by the precise subset and labels of loop coordinates yields an honest direct-sum integral chain isomorphism to shifted tree-anchored chains. The established tree homotopy theorem (Kozlov Theorem 2.5) computes all summands, including r=1 contractibility and n=r disjoint r!-point cases. The formula follows by degree accounting without extension problems. Fourteen exact independent cubical mod-two chain-rank comparisons agree; these finite tests are explicitly not presented as an infinite or integral proof.

originality.rationale: The decisive recent primary text arXiv:2609.04554v1 explicitly calls integral torsion in anchored graph configuration spaces unresolved; its proven cograph finite-generation and torsion-exponent bounds do not imply torsion-freeness or ranks. The older Stirling theorem proves the tree case and its appendix only extends to contractible ambient complexes, so it does not imply the noncontractible loop splitting. Kozlov 2024 gives all-graph Euler characteristic but full homology only for circle graphs. Targeted actual index and literature searches and owned claim-level comparisons identified no equivalent statement; no exhaustive assertion about unpublished literature is made.
residual_risks: An equivalent result might exist in unpublished or unindexed literature; semantic search and three directly relevant primary full texts do not prove worldwide uniqueness.
Homological torsion-freeness does not determine cohomology products or homotopy type; no such stronger conclusion is claimed.

value.rationale: The originating 2026 paper explicitly identifies unknown integral torsion beyond trees and circles and provides only bounded torsion exponents for cographs. The result resolves this existence question for every connected graph and computes all integral Betti ranks uniformly using only b,r,n, revealing a structural chain decomposition. This is a substantive topology theorem, neither a routine Euler-characteristic deduction nor a narrowly motivated numerical gain. It also supplies a computable model without expanding arbitrary large graph-product matrices.
